title: Add Vaporize JSON Schema fixture validation for schema-universal expected-pass and expected-fail records
createdBy: codex after chairman required a governed vaporware modification request

historicalContent.sourceLocation: Codex session 2026-07-04: chairman rejected jq as authoritative schema fixture proof and required an entire Vaporware Modification Request before implementation.
historicalContent.description: Vaporize needs a first-class JSON Schema fixture validation command so schema-backed release evidence can prove both expected-pass and expected-fail fixtures without ad hoc jq checks. The first proof set is schema-universal workstream-schemas v0.0.4, whose fixtures distinguish ongoing workstreams, temporary initiatives, summaries, and invalid lifecycle classifications.
acceptanceCriteria: Vaporize exposes validate-json-schema with --schema, --fixture, and --expect pass|fail.
The command exits 0 only when the actual schema validation result matches the declared expectation.
The command exits nonzero when the fixture fails an expected-pass check or unexpectedly passes an expected-fail check.
The command emits or can write a structured receipt naming schema path, fixture path, expectation, actual result, diagnostics, and next steps.
The implementation supports the local reference and draft vocabulary needs of workstream-schemas v0.0.4 before that fixture set is claimed as proved.
CUJ-06 Swift Testing coverage exercises JSON syntax validation, expected-pass schema validation, expected-fail schema validation, expectation mismatch, and actionable failure output.
No XCTest target is introduced for this slice.
Release evidence names the new schema-backed fixture validation obligation or explicitly records why release-doctor enforcement is deferred.
Every command error includes robust next steps, procedure or evidence links, and guidance to bring the error to Digikoma when the operator cannot proceed.
The prior jq semantic fixture check is not used as the authoritative release proof.
knownSeparations: This bead owns the Vaporize command and release proof lane, not the schema-universal workstream schema semantics.
schema-universal owns the schema files, fixture records, and schema migrator semantics.
The initial command may scope to local schemas and local references; remote schema fetching is not part of the first acceptance slice.
The existing validate-json repeated --path bug can be fixed alongside this work, but it is not a substitute for schema instance validation.
The bead is filed at the Vaporize owner home first; a job-board projection should reference this bead when a Vaporize implementation board is opened.

progressNotes.note: validate-json-schema mode landed: sources/vaporize-cli/JSONSchemaValidation.swift (draft-2020-12 subset engine: type/properties/required/additionalProperties/const/enum/allOf/anyOf/oneOf/if-then-else/items/minItems/minLength/minimum/$defs; $ref internal pointers + local relative-file refs with canonical-path caching and cycle guard; remote http(s) $ref raises actionable unsupported-schema-feature error). CLI wiring in main.swift: Mode.validateJSONSchema, --schema/--fixture/--expect (ExpectOutcome pass|fail), JSONSchemaValidationReceipt (receiptKind vaporize-json-schema-validation) emitted via emitReceiptIfRequested, and VaporizeCLIActionability.schemaValidationMessage naming schema path, fixture path, expectation, actual, diagnostics, next steps, and the Digikoma triage command with existing policy/procedure/digikoma refs.
evidence: swift test --filter VaporizeCUJ06JSONValidationTests: 8 tests passed (3 prior JSON-syntax tests kept + 5 new CUJ-06 schema tests: expected-pass, expected-fail with diagnostics, expectation mismatch, actionable failure message, remote-$ref rejection)

Live nine-fixture matrix against workstream-schemas v0.0.4: 4 canonical fixtures --expect pass exit 0; 5 invalid fixtures --expect fail exit 0; invalid fixture with --expect pass exits 64 with the actionable message; receipt emission proved via --receipt-path

progressNotes.note: Schema-side fix required for the proof set: workstream.schema.json and workstream-summary.schema.json (plus their versions/0.0.4 copies) in schema-universal carried dangling relative $refs to primitives/schema-primitives (7 x ../ where the on-disk layout at domain/primitives requires 8 x ../; versions copies 9 -> 10). Fixed in place and verified all ref targets resolve. Sibling schemas workstream-contribution.schema.json and workstream-moment.schema.json (and their versions copies) still carry the same dangling-primitives-$ref bug; they are outside this fixture proof set and remain for schema-universal to fix.

Release evidence: cuj-test-coverage.json/.md updated (VaporizeCUJ06JSONValidationTests 3 -> 8, currentExecutableSwiftTestCount 155 -> 160) and the CUJ-09 counter expectation updated to 160; the CUJ-09 coverage-contract test passes. NOT done yet: release-gates/release-doctor enforcement naming the schema-backed fixture validation obligation (acceptance criterion 8) is still pending, and the prior validate-json multiple --path bug remains open in its own bead. Pre-existing unrelated failure noted honestly: CUJ-09 'product definition contract precedes build work' fails at HEAD because feature-catalog.md no longer contains 'Xcode-selected Swift toolchain' (removed by commit a223620d in the FR-VAPORIZE-DOCC-TOOLCHAIN-BRIDGE-2026-07-05 workstream); not caused by and not force-fixed in this slice.

Attached the Schema Universal Ontology Inspector Spawn-request correction to this existing governed validation cohort. JSONSchemaValidation now enforces array contains. The current-source Vaporize executable accepted the owned v0.0.5 Spawn request, including its SwiftUI and pixel-spec contains commitments, and rejected an independent nonmatching array with the contains diagnostic. CUJ-06 gained a durable contains pass/fail case. The focused SwiftPM test target was invoked but did not reach the test because SwiftPM materialized the package-wide test-bundle graph, exhausted the local volume, and hit an unrelated Xcode code-signing subsystem error; no test-pass claim is made from that attempt.
